html:
Lan Na, "a million rice fields", was a Tai kingdom in what is now northern Thailand, from the late 1200s to the 1700s. Its founder Mangrai took the old Mon kingdom of Haripunchai in 1292 and built Chiang Mai as his capital in 1296. Lan Na had its own script and its own school of Theravada Buddhism.

Under King Tilokarat in the 1400s it was strong enough to fight Ayutthaya on equal terms, and in 1477 Chiang Mai hosted a great council of Buddhist monks. It weakened after that. In 1558 Bayinnaung of Burma made it a vassal, and for about two centuries it was ruled by vassal kings under Burmese control. The map's snapshots from 1600 to 1715 show it in this period.

In 1775 the local lord Kawila, with help from Siam, drove out the Burmese. Lan Na became a vassal of Siam, later the Rattanakosin Kingdom, and was fully absorbed in the late 1800s.
